description: Phase transition of a linear one-hidden-layer net in the spatial dimension d and the prior strength: spatial.d in {1, 2, 3, 4} x spatial.lambda_max in {0.1, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99} (20 settings, d slowest), phi id, L = 1, SGLD, float64, MIR monitor, the sizes of `spatial_exp`, and an ensemble of B = 8 networks per setting (net.B is a one-value axis, so no other exp.json gains a field). Every population is embedded at random (uniform on the d-torus, seed 0, so the members of an ensemble share one geometry), which makes any N valid in any d; the wrapped Gaussian is a product over the axes, so every kernel is PSD. All populations have length scale 0.15. Each kernel is rescaled to top eigenvalue lambda_max, so the per-weight prior variance shrinks with the population size; weight_lambda is 1 (the `Config` rule under lambda_max). SGLD at lr 1e-2: the prior's stiffest curvature k grows like 1 / (min_rel_eig lambda_max)^2, and the stability check passes everywhere, but at lambda_max 0.1 (d <= 3) lr * k = 1 on the stiffest modes, so Euler-Maruyama doubles their variance (prior power inflated by up to about 13% at d = 1). The softest prior mode relaxes on about 2e6 lambda_max^2 epochs (1e4 at 0.1, 1e6 at 0.99), so at 250k epochs settings with lambda_max >= 0.5 are not fully stationary from the N(0, 1) initialisation.
